source_text:
16.3 ̓Εδοκίμασας τὴν καρδίαν μου, ἐπεσ κέψω νυκτός. Εἰ ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν
κατεργάζεται, ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμασίαν, ἡ θλῖψις α ρα δο κιμασίαν κατεργάζεται· εἰ
δὲ ἡ δοκιμα σία ἐν νυκτὶ διέδραμεν, ἡ νὺξ ἐνταῦθα τὴν θλῖψιν σημαίνει, ἐν ῃ
σκοτοῦται πταιομένη ψυχὴ λογική. –Εἰσέλθετε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης καὶ
τεθλιμμένης ὁδοῦ, τουτέστι τῆς πρακτικῆς, η τις δοκεῖ πρῶτον ὀδύνης, καὶ οὐ
χαρᾶς πρόξενος, υ στερον μέντοι καρποὺς δικαιοσύνης ἀποδιδοῦσα τοῖς δι' αὐτῆς γε
γυμνασμένοις.
pass_a_gloss: You-tested the heart of-me, you-visited of-night. If the affliction patience works-out, and the patience testing, the affliction then testing works-out; if but the testing in night ran-through, the night here the affliction signifies, in-which is-darkened stumbling soul rational. Enter through the narrow gate and afflicted way, that-is of-the practical, which-one seems first of-pain, and not of-joy bringer, later however fruits of-righteousness giving-back to-the through it having-been-trained.
pass_b_english: “You tested my heart; you visited by night” (Psalm 16:3).

If affliction works patience, and patience testing, then affliction works testing. And if the testing ran its course in night, the night here signifies the affliction, in which a stumbling rational soul is darkened.

“Enter through the narrow gate and the afflicted way”: that is, the practical life, which seems at first a bringer of pain and not of joy, but afterward giving back fruits of righteousness to those trained through it.

choices.term: ἡ νὺξ ἐνταῦθα τὴν θλῖψιν σημαίνει
choices.english: the night here signifies the affliction
choices.why: Night is not clock-time only; it is the affliction in which the rational soul is darkened.
rejected: night signifies testing only, not affliction

choices.english: a stumbling rational soul is darkened
choices.why: πταιομένη is the soul stumbling. Not ‘a darkened soul that was struck’.
rejected: the rational soul darkens the stumble

choices.why: πρακτική is Origen’s practical life, the afflicted way. Not ‘practice’ as rehearsal.
rejected: that is, of the practical gate only

choices.term: ὕστερον μέντοι καρποὺς δικαιοσύνης ἀποδιδοῦσα τοῖς δι’ αὐτῆς γεγυμνασμένοις
choices.english: afterward giving back fruits of righteousness to those trained through it
choices.why: Hebrews 12:11. OCR υ στερον / γε γυμνασμένοις. Not ‘later it gives joy instead of fruit’.
rejected: it gives fruits to those untrained
